messages.author: 53b7f8e786284601
messages.subject: Problem Configuring RApache on OS X 10.5.8
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I've been trying to get RApache set up properly on my Macbook Pro
running OS X 10.5.8. After installing RApache successfully (I think),
I added the following to the httpd.conf file as suggested.

# All Apache modules are loaded this way. The most important thing to
# remember is that the string "R_module" is case sensitive, so get it
# right in the config file.

LoadModule R_module /apache/module/path/mod_R.so

# Place this in the config file to turn error messages into HTML which
# are printed in the browser. Without this, all warning and error
messages
# are printed to the Apache error log file.

ROutputErrors

# Prints out a nice report about R running within Apache
<Location /RApacheInfo>
SetHandler r-info
</Location>

With these additions, I was then able to successfully go to
http://localhost/RApacheInfo and see the status information.
If I add the following additional line,

REvalOnStartup "library(brew)"

I can no longer successfully load the RApacheInfo page successfully.
I don't know what the issue is here.

Any thoughts as to what I might be doing wrong?

Chris

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Re: Problem Configuring RApache on OS X 10.5.8
parts:
Hi Chris,

Your email looks almost verbatim like JD Long's question on SO...

I've posted a reply there but will copy it here:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2344368/problem-configuring-rapache-on-os-x-10-5-8

I'm not sure why you're getting this error on just loading a library,
but we've seen this issue on Leopard due to Apple's freetype/
fontconfig/cairo libraries calling CoreFoundation calls:

http://finzi.psych.upenn.edu/R/Rhelp02/archive/118681.html

How did you install R?

I tried reproducing your issue on Snow Leopard with stock apache2,
binary R 2.10.1 from CRAN, Xcode 3.2.1, and rapche 1.1.8 but no luck.
My setup worked like a champ.

I don't have access to Leopard anymore, so my best suggestion is to
use gdb to break on that really long system call. You will want to
remove the REvalonStartup directive and replace it with a handler call
which does the same, configure apache to spawn only one child process
(hence the whole fork thing) and connect gdb to it. Then point your
web browser to your handler url and see if gdb breaks on the function
and then look at the stack trace.... Pretty lame I know, but that's
all I got for now.
